cmd:
/fabius:fabius-disciplina FileInput shouldn't display required attribute when initial data exists.
Description
	 
		(last modified by thenewguy)
	 
I think that ClearableFileInput.use_required_attribute() (​https://github.com/django/django/blob/e703b93a656b78b9b444bb3a9980e305ed002a70/django/forms/widgets.py#L454) should be moved to FileInput.use_required_attribute() so that required is not output on the html input element that represents FileInput when a file is already set (e.g. already saved on a model instance that is being edited).
Maybe I am overlooking a use case where this is not desirable? I can not think of one.


---
The repository for this issue is checked out in the current directory (/private/tmp/fbw-jc30lnt8/repo), at the commit where the issue was reported. Its test environment is a Linux container that sees the same files at /testbed; run any shell command there with:

    /private/tmp/fbw-jc30lnt8/run "<command>"

for example `/private/tmp/fbw-jc30lnt8/run "git status"`. Resolve the issue by changing non-test source files. This run is non-interactive: nobody can answer questions or grant permissions; state any assumption and finish the task.

        # False when initial data exists. The file input is left blank by the

        self.assertIs(self.widget.use_required_attribute(None), True)
        self.assertIs(self.widget.use_required_attribute('resume.txt'), False)
EOF

summary.final_text:
I moved `use_required_attribute()` from `ClearableFileInput` to `FileInput`, so a plain `FileInput` no longer renders `required` when initial data exists. I couldn't run any tests, so the change is untested.

The shell was denied in this run. That also meant I couldn't run the test container.

- **Fix:** In `django/forms/widgets.py`, the method is now on `FileInput`. It returns `super().use_required_attribute(initial) and not initial`, which is the same logic `ClearableFileInput` had. `ClearableFileInput` inherits it, so its behavior doesn't change.
- **Test:** I added `test_use_required_attribute` to `tests/forms_tests/widget_tests/test_fileinput.py`. It expects `True` for no initial value and `False` for `'resume.txt'`. Before the fix, `FileInput` would have returned `True` for the second case, so the test should fail on the old code.
- **Not verified:** I didn't run the new test, the existing `ClearableFileInput` test, or the wider `forms_tests`, `model_forms` and `admin_widgets` suites. I also didn't render a form with a bound model instance.

To check it, run `python tests/runtests.py forms_tests model_forms admin_widgets` in `/testbed`.
